statements.text: AI is no longer a technology of the future. It is already changing how main street does business. [...] There is a broad bipartisan agreement that America should lead the world in AI innovation. But leadership also requires rules of the road. That is where Congress has fallen short. We still don't have a clear national framework for AI governance that addresses safety, innovation, and equal opportunity.
statements.venue: House Small Business Committee hearing 'AI on Main Street' opening remarks

statements.text: The largest corporations already have the resources to adopt AI, manage compliance, and pay for future subscription costs. Many small businesses do not. If we fail to close that gap, AI could accelerate market concentration and leave main street struggling to compete. [...] Congress needs to invest in AI literacy and establish thoughtful federal guardrails to ensure that AI becomes a tool for innovation and opportunity, and not another barrier to success.
statements.venue: House Small Business Committee hearing 'AI on Main Street' opening remarks

statements.text: AI is already changing how Main Street does business, and we need to make sure that this technology works for everyone, not just large corporations. AI should be a tool for innovation and opportunity, not a barrier to success. https://t.co/MgDdQdO3AK

We write to urge you to keep the House of Representatives in session to enable Congress to take urgent action to address the catastrophic risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. Those risks take any of several forms, separately and in combination—of agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons.
statements.venue: Joint letter to Speaker Johnson signed by Tran

statements.text: We have a responsibility to be mindful and fully aware of the risks associated with A.I., including rising utility costs for consumers and small business owners. As a former consumer protection attorney, I am deeply concerned that our communities are currently the ones who pay the price for new data centers. The Ratepayer Protection Act protects hardworking families from these costs by ensuring that the data centers are the ones who pay for energy and grid upgrades, not the other way around.
statements.venue: Official press release on Ratepayer Protection Act vote

statements.text: As data center development grows throughout the country, Congress must address the rising energy costs associated with their development. [...] I believe AI has its advantages, including the ability to create good paying union jobs, but appropriate oversight and regulation is key to keeping this rapidly evolving industry in check. We must continue to develop policies that hold the companies building these data centers accountable.
